rows.gloss: cloth, woven silk; bandage, fillet turban, diadem
rows.etymology: 7700 paṭṭa² m. 'cloth, woven silk' Kāv., 'bandage, fillet turban, diadem' MBh. [Prob. like paṭa- and *phēṭṭa-¹ from non-Aryan source, of which *patta- in Gy. and *patra- in Sh. may represent aryanization of paṭṭa-. Not < páttra- nor, with P. Tedesco Archaeologica Orientalia in Memoriam Ernst Herzfeld 222, < *pr̥ṣṭa- 'woven', while an assumed borrowing from IA. in Bur. phΛlto-čiṅ 'puttees' is too flimsy a basis for *palta- (~ Eng. fold, &c.) as the source NTS xiii 93]

references.source:
Dave Beine\.
A sociolinguistic survey of the bhatri\-speaking communities of central india\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2017\-005, SIL International, 5 2017\.
Researched by Dave Beine, Bruce Cain, Kathy Cain, Michael Jeyabalan, Ashok Sawlikar and Satya Soren\. Fieldwork was carried out between February and November 1989 in Bastar District, Madhya Pradesh \(now Chhattisgarh\) and Koraput District, Orissa \(now Odisha\), and the report was published without revision in May 2017\. Word lists of 210 items were elicited at each site in what the report calls a modified International Phonetic Alphabet; no transcription key is printed, so the symbol values recorded in conversion/beine\-bhatri\.txt are established distributionally and from the rendered page images\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/resources/archives/71330](https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/71330)\.
references.progress: Appendix A: Wordlists only (PDF pages 16--39 = printed pages 10--33): the complete 12 site x 210 concept comparative word list, comprising nine Bhatri survey points and the three comparison lects (Halbi from Bhatpal, Oriya from Cuttack, Adivasi Oriya from Araku Valley). 2,444 of the 2,520 printed cells carry an elicited word and yield 2,492 installed forms, 48 of them second responses printed in one cell; 74 cells print an en dash and 2 Halbi cells print a stray combining mark, and all 76 are recorded as missing in the audit. The report body, Appendix B (narrative texts and comprehension questions), Appendix C (recorded-text-test score sheets) and the References are not installed
references.provenance: Extracted from the born-digital CharisSIL text layer of the published PDF (SHA-256 4a9fec255be6a5e9967b66c494a4be575599d39bce58609573733a51a09d2891) with the reproducible importer data/other/forms/raw_data/beine_bhatri.py; checked-in audit data/other/forms/raw_data/20260825-beine-bhatri-audit.csv, manifest 20260825-beine-bhatri-manifest.json and seeded sample 20260825-beine-bhatri-sample.csv; installed rows in data/other/forms/20260825-beine-bhatri.csv; transcription profile conversion/beine-bhatri.txt

language.name: Indo-Aryan
language.map_marker: <svg viewBox="0 0 30 30" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><polygon points="0,15 15,0 30,15 15,30" fill="#E2DFD2" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

references.source:
Bijumon Varghese, Mathews John, and Nelson Samuel\.
The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009\-011, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 9 2009\.
The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. Printed source metadata provide localities and administrative units but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect rows intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009\-011\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009-011.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix B, printed pages 59--177: 6,894 lexical responses from thirty Malvi target lists grouped by the source as Ujjaini, Rajwadi, Umadwadi, Sondhwadi, Gond-Malvi and Bhil-Malvi. Excludes 37 target cells printed as "By Name" rather than a lexical form, two Bhili and two Nimadi comparison lists, the Bhopali comparison list, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standards, ten explicit no-entry control cells, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine and 24 feces which the report says were disqualified and removed
references.provenance: The exact official publisher PDF was recovered through Internet Archive capture 20150930085157 because the legacy SIL URL no longer serves the file directly; PDF SHA-256 e67e314974ab10eb8244b08dba56d08d1ce8cbf16eaef1be022071d49032a2dd. The PDF is not redistributed. Reproducible font decoding, geometric extraction and checked snapshot are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_malvi_2009; complete per-record audit is data/other/forms/raw_data/20260828-sil-malvi-audit.csv; installed rows are data/other/forms/20260828-sil-malvi.csv

rows.etymology: 1358. Bng. lɔṭi-pɔṭi n.f. ‘household effects, possessions’, Cam. laṭā phaṭā ‘property, goods’, Ku. laṭpaṭi ‘property, possessions’, Garh. laṭṭi-paṭṭi ‘sājo-sāmān – joint possessions’ and laṭar-paṭar ‘belongings, petty things’, P. laṭā-paṭā ‘furniture, goods’ — Western Marw. lōthī-pōthī ‘property’, Jaṭ. laṭā-paṭā ‘baggage, furniture, effects’ < OIA *lap- tra- ‘possessions’ (10938) with modern parallels in Kt., Pr., Dm., Sh. to which is to be added M. kapḍālattā ‘clothes and other things’. Note: Here also Chin. lach-goru ‘cattle’ (with second component < OIA gorūpá- ‘cow-shaped’ [4313]) — Sh. lac̣ ‘goat, he-goat; herd (of goats)’. Whereas Kal. eċī ‘cow’, Ks. bič ‘cow’, Bur.ys. veċ ‘cow half year after delivery’ and Gaw. eċí̄ ‘cow’ do not rectilineal derive, as suggested by Turner and Morgenstierne (1950b), < OIA vatsá-¹ ‘calf’ (11239), but most probably got mixed up with reflexes of PIE *h1eˆgh- ‘cow’ (see p. 783), Kho. lˈešu ‘cow’ (note also lešpˈay ‘livestock’ with second component “milk” see p. 643) is perhaps an amalgamation of the PIE lemma and OIA *laptra-.
